about: The compile flags of every lean_mpas build, read by tools/lean/config.py. A unit's options are common + profile (with omp) + the unit_rules that match it, in this order; its defines are defines + the build switches + the defines of the matching rules.

omp.why: -fopenmp right after -O0 in the debug profile; in every other profile it comes last. The order changes no code.

o3native.why: -O3 for the build machine's own CPU.

fast.why: the CPU performance build, by compile classes (compile_classes): kernels -O3 for the build machine's own CPU (FMA contraction on, gfortran's default), infrastructure -O2. Athens 3 km, 8 threads on 8 cores of one kind, 100 steps, run time as a fraction of envelope o3's: -O3 -march=native by classes 0.94 (two repeated runs within 0.2%); + the level count fixed at build time (./lean build --levels 45) 0.88; + -fno-math-errno -funroll-loops 0.86 (2.4% less; each alone was under the 2% margin: 0.9% and 1.7% less than -O3 -march=native by classes). Sane after 100 steps: LEAN OK, no NaN, T2 against o3 rms 0.04 K (max 0.9 K, one cell), 10 m wind rms 0.01 m/s.

gfortran.variants_why: per profile (envelope, fast), the variants that --variant names. A variant's flags take the place of the profile flags; common flags, omp and the unit rules stay. A variant with classes instead of flags gives one flag set per compile class (compile_classes): each unit takes the set of its class, the link takes the kernel set. flags is a list, or one list per machine (arm64, x86_64: tools/lean/config.py machine()). status: envelope (a legitimate build; the spread of these builds' forecasts is the envelope a faster build must stay within) or supported (with the platforms it passed on).

profiles_why.debug: -Mbounds checks array bounds and -Ktrap=fp traps invalid, divide-by-zero and overflow. nvfortran has no signalling-NaN initialisation like gfortran's -finit-real=snan, so an uninitialised real is not caught as it is in the gfortran debug build. The card debug build is these flags with the card rules applied, as for strict.

profiles_why.strict: value-safe Intel build: no reassociation, no contraction to FMA; not bit-identical with gfortran or nvfortran, only checked against them by forecast.
profiles_why.debug: -check enables every run-time check (bounds, pointers, uninitialised), -fpe0 traps invalid, divide-by-zero and overflow.

omp.why: -qopenmp after the profile flags, as -fopenmp for gfortran.

fast.why: the Intel CPU performance build by compile classes: kernels -O3 for the build machine's CPU (ifx's default -fp-model fast), infrastructure -O2, phys_state -O0 (reduced). Athens 3 km, 8 threads on 8 cores of one kind, 100 steps, run time as a fraction of gfortran fast's with the same level setting: 0.86 without and 0.89 with the level count fixed at build time (--levels 45); 0.81 and 0.77 of gfortran envelope o3's. Sane after 100 steps: LEAN OK, no NaN, T2 against gfortran o3 rms 0.04 K (max 0.8 K), 10 m wind rms 0.01 m/s. A run needs /opt/intel/oneapi/compiler/<version>/lib on LD_LIBRARY_PATH (libimf, libiomp5).

compile_classes.about: Compile classes, after WRF's configure.wrf (FCOPTIM, FCNOOPT, FCREDUCEDOPT): a variant with classes gives each class its own flag set. kernel: the dynamics and physics that run every step (the default); infrastructure: input/output, configuration, start-up, readers, CLI glue, which run once or at output times; reduced: named exceptions a compiler cannot optimise fully, each with its why. The first member entry that names a unit (or its group) decides its class; an entry with fc applies to that compiler only. Builds without classes (strict, debug, envelope and the fast variants that give flags) ignore this table. The unit_rules still add their options on top of every class.

members.why: ifx 2025.2 had not finished this generated unit at -O3 -xHost or at -O1 (8.8 GB of memory) when stopped, after more than 300 times what -O0 needs. On the CPU it holds the zeros and copies of the physics state, no per-step loop.
the MPAS ESMF time manager: clock arithmetic a few times a step.

configuration, namelists, messages and logs, streams, start-up from the init file, the readers and writers of netCDF, restart, products, the command line: they run once or at output times, none has an OpenMP loop.

unit_rule_groups_why: a rule that names units matches them only in these groups: the Noah-MP and ESMF closures get only the flags of the group rules below.

unit_rules.why: nvfortran 25.3 inliner ICE on this file at -O2.
-Mnovect only on the Grell-Freitas and GWDO units: needed for bit identity with MPAS's original Grell-Freitas and GWDO code under nvfortran.
OpenACC on the card units: the dynamics, the device physics and radiation from src/device, and phys_fault, lean_warp.

Thompson's card stages at most 128 registers a thread (thompson, dyn_micro): its stage mp_thompson_b1 held 254 (its 56 double-precision rates), two blocks of 128 a multiprocessor; with the spills it takes about 30 % less time on a 120 km global mesh, with the same bits (registers only).
the card build runs the device physics (src/phys_dev.f90).
exner power on the card: double precision plus the host library for the cells near a rounding midpoint.
the lean Noah-MP code is compiled with -std=f2018 under gfortran.
the device Noah-MP code (src/device) is compiled with OpenACC, without -Minfo.
the MPAS ESMF time manager is compiled without MPI.
